open_obligations: Note that easy-to-hard (correct labels on easy data) and weak-to-strong (noisy labels from a weaker model) are different setups.
Check whether Hase et al. tested reward modeling, where Burns et al.'s result is weakest.
Do not read either result as transferring to the other's setting.
in.other_title: Weak-to-strong generalization is poor on ChatGPT reward modeling (about 10% PGR)
in.rationale: Hase et al. suggest from strong easy-to-hard generalization that scalable oversight may be easier than previously thought. Burns et al. report naive weak-to-strong generalization on ChatGPT reward modeling recovers only about 10% of the gap (almost never above 20%) and say their results suggest that naively using weak, human-level supervision will be insufficient to align strong, superhuman models; the two vary different axes (label difficulty versus supervisor strength).
in.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: whether limited or weaker supervision is sufficient to elicit strong models' capabilities, i.e. whether scalable oversight is easier than thought
